description: Document Phase-6a and RETIRE Phase-6b from the roadmap. Add the Local Sharing architecture section (four capabilities + plugin contract + profile precedence + manifest); extend the adapters README with the plugin/extension contract; add USAGE instructions for the four capabilities AND accurate end-to-end instructions for exercising ALL accumulated APIA features in VS Code and Visual Studio 2022 (the user's next step is real-IDE validation); record executed PROOF; update README; and rewrite the roadmap so it ENDS cleanly at local git-based sharing with external/hosted sharing stated as intentionally OUT OF SCOPE (remove former Phase-6b 'deferred/coming' wording). Depends on FEAT-002 and FEAT-003.
steps: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: add a 'Local Sharing (Phase 6a)' section describing the four capabilities (versioned knowledge packs with safe no-clobber merge; shared org/team profiles layered onto config.yml with LOCAL-overrides-win precedence; the local plugin/extension contract for adapters/scanners/shapes as committed files; the capability manifest reusing doctor + detection), each framed honestly as LOCAL git-based sharing. Make a DELIVERED (Phase 6a) roadmap bullet in the same style as the existing DELIVERED (Phase 1-5) bullets.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md ROADMAP CLEANUP: remove/replace the former external-platform wording. Specifically rewrite the 'DEFERRED - Cross-team / org knowledge & capability sharing + plugins' bullet and the 'Phase 4 - Knowledge & capability sharing (high level)' section (the one naming a shared knowledge-base SERVICE, an MCP server exposing APIA to other agents, cross-org/external APIs, collaborative workspaces, and marketplace distribution) so that: (a) LOCAL git-based sharing is DELIVERED in Phase 6a; (b) external/hosted/cross-org sharing (MCP servers exposing APIA, cross-org APIs, collaborative-workspace services, marketplace distribution) is stated as intentionally OUT OF SCOPE for APIA - a separate product with its own security/hosting/governance model - NOT merely deferred/coming later. The roadmap must END cleanly at local git-based sharing. Keep the OTHER genuinely-deferred items (C#/Groovy adapters stubs; MCP DATA sources; auto-push/PR/MR/CI/packaging/signing; the optional self-hosted second-opinion reviewer) labeled as before.

.apia/adapters/README.md: extend with a 'Local plugins / extensions' section documenting the exact plugin directory under .apia/, the contract for each plugin type (adapter YAML schema already documented here; scanner via the scanners: contract; shape/template via scaffold's shape ids + generate.templates), how the off-model scripts DISCOVER and LOAD plugins, the no-download/no-remote/no-marketplace invariant, and the malformed-plugin graceful-failure behavior. Must match what FEAT-002 actually implemented.

USAGE.md: add a 'Local sharing' section with concrete command recipes for export/import a knowledge pack (incl. the safe no-clobber behavior and --force), apply an org/team profile (precedence), add a local plugin, and query capabilities (--manifest/--plugins/--doctor, --json). ALSO add/refresh clear, accurate instructions for exercising ALL accumulated APIA features (ingest, feature loop, C++, eval/iterate, reviewer, generation, orchestrator, iterate-to-best, and this sharing layer) in BOTH VS Code (Agent Host: Tier-0 + prompts + skills + agents) and Visual Studio 2022 (Tier-0 + Tier-1 prompts only - name which prompts carry each flow). Update the deferred-features note in USAGE.md to reflect 6b being out of scope.

docs/PROOF.md: add a Phase-6a section recording the FOR-REAL executed evidence from FEAT-002's tests/CLI: the knowledge-pack round-trip (artifacts/project-facts match), the safe-merge no-clobber (and force override), version-field handling, profile apply + precedence (local wins), local plugin discovery/load for an adapter + a scanner (+ shape if done) incl. the malformed graceful-failure, and the capability manifest content (adapters complete-vs-stub, scanners, shapes, plugins, versions) for both Python and C++ where relevant. State honestly that these mechanics are fully executed in-sandbox (no live-model dependency for Phase-6a mechanics).

README.md: add a brief mention of the local sharing layer (packs/profiles/plugins/manifest) and update any roadmap/status line so it reflects that APIA's roadmap ends at local git-based sharing with external/hosted sharing out of scope.

Grep the repo for lingering 'Phase 6b' / 'coming later' / 'deferred ... external platform/cross-org/marketplace/MCP server exposing APIA' wording and reconcile it with the out-of-scope framing (do NOT touch the legitimately-deferred MCP DATA-source and self-hosted-reviewer notes).
